Routine yearly exam.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Christine is a 63-year-old female presenting for her routine yearly examination. She reports doing well overall. Regarding her depression, she states she has been managing well with her prescribed medication and weekly therapy sessions, sleeping a full eight hours nightly, with no suicidal ideation. She denies any concerning symptoms related to her depression. 

Regarding her hypertension, she reports checking her blood pressure at home, which has been fluctuating between high and low readings over the past couple of weeks without remaining stable. She confirms adherence to her blood pressure medication. She attributes recent stress at work and increased hours to dietary changes, reporting she has been eating frozen meals due to lack of time for grocery shopping and meal preparation. She reports occasional headaches which she attributes to prolonged computer screen time. She denies numbness or tingling in her hands or fingers. Regarding her carpal tunnel release performed on her right wrist approximately two years ago, she reports it has been doing well.
